content: RBMS1, also known as RNA-binding motif, single-stranded-interacting protein 1, is a protein encoded by the RBMS1 gene in humans. This gene encodes a member of a small family of proteins that specifically bind to single-stranded DNA or RNA. These proteins are characterized by the presence of two ribonucleoprotein consensus sequence (RNP-CS) motifs, known as RNP1 and RNP2. These motifs are conserved sequences originally identified in RNA-binding proteins and are essential for DNA-binding activity. RBMS1 proteins are implicated in a variety of cellular functions, including DNA replication, gene transcription, cell cycle progression, and apoptosis. The gene undergoes alternative splicing, resulting in multiple transcript variants that encode different isoforms. Some of these isoforms were identified based on their ability to bind to either strand of an upstream regulatory element of the c-myc gene (referred to as MSSPs), through phenotypic complementation of yeast mutants cdc2 and cdc13 (referred to as scr2), or as a potential human repressor of HIV-1 and ILR-2 alpha promoter transcription (referred to as YC1). Additionally, a pseudogene corresponding to RBMS1 is located on chromosome 12. RBMS1 has been demonstrated to interact with DNA polymerase alpha 1, a key enzyme involved in DNA replication.
